content.text: Ten-second uninterrupted live-action historical camp rescue, full-frame16:9. Single reference shows the SAME living injured young soldier sitting alone against the cart wheel, no contact yet. Camera is the rescuer's FIRST PERSON eyes throughout, never show a third-person rescuer or camera operator. At first approach and crouch smoothly. At3 seconds the rescuer's RIGHT forearm enters from bottom right, pale blue-white sleeve with worn silver-gray bracer, hand open. A young adult male voice at camera position says ONLY “拉住我。” once in clear Mandarin; the injured soldier's mouth does not form these words. Injured soldier looks at hand then uses BOTH his hands to grip rescuer's forearm, contact stabilizes. Only after grip, lift gently so his shoulders/back separate from the cart and he begins to rise, with real fabric tension and arm weight. Five fingers per hand, no added rescuers or extra arms. Natural effort breathing by both people, boots and cloth, distant fire. No extra dialogue, no voiceover reading directions, no music, no subtitles, no black borders.
